summary_paragraph: A woman with multiple comorbidities, including severe COPD, diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, obesity hypoventilation syndrome, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted due to altered mental status and hypoxia. She was found agitated and noncompliant with oxygen at her nursing home, leading to respiratory acidosis and acute kidney injury. She required intubation for hypercapnic respiratory failure but was extubated the next day. Encephalopathy was attributed to hypercarbia and accumulation of opioid metabolites due to reduced kidney function. Her kidney injury resolved with IV fluids and medication adjustments. A urinary tract infection was suspected initially, but cultures grew only yeast, so antibiotics were discontinued. She was stabilized on home oxygen, her pain regimen was simplified to avoid sedating opioids, and she was discharged to extended care with improved mental status and renal function.
